newsitem.title: USA: Central Sprinkler drops on test reports.
newsitem.headline: Central Sprinkler drops on test reports.

text.p: Shares of Central Sprinkler Corp dropped sharply on Wednesday after media reports said a type of fire-sprinkler head produced by the Lansdale, Pa., company failed to work properly.
Central Sprinkler lost 2-3/4 to 17-1/4 in early afternoon trading.

A media report issued Tuesday said a model of the Omega sprinkler produced by Central Sprinkler has a 31 percent failure rate in ongoing Underwriters Laboratories tests and a 35 percent failure rate in tests conducted for a Fairfax, Va. county fire and rescue department.

Central Sprinkler said those tests were on an old sprinkler head model that is no longer produced. The company also said those tests monitored the sprinkler head under unusual conditions, instead of normal operating conditions.
Central Sprinkler said it first discovered problems with that sprinkler model after a May 1995 fire at a Marriott Courtyard hotel in Michigan.

"Central Sprinkler investigated the problem, pinpointed it and notified its customers of the problem. We acted aggressively in offering kits to retrofit the sprinkler," said Judy Leon, a spokeswoman for Central Sprinkler.
She said the company has spent $4 million on the problem.

Central Sprinkler said the problem affected only a limited number of sprinklers that contained a rubber part, called an O-ring. The company switched materials used to make the part, which eliminated the problem, Leon said.

Although the faulty model is no longer made, some of the sprinklers may still be in use since some customers have not retrofitted the product, Leon said. But the company said it did not know how many of those sprinklers were still in use.
Central Sprinkler said it continues to offer retro-fitting kits for customers using that Omega model.
